name: MOTO-HUB
subtitle: A ride dashboard for motorcycles with an EasyConn screen
description:
MOTO-HUB turns an iPhone into the navigation and ride display for motorcycles whose dashboard speaks the EasyConn/Carbit protocol — CFMOTO, Voge, Zontes, Moto Morini, Benelli, KOVE, QJ Motor and others. The phone draws a map, speed, navigation and trip data and projects it onto the motorcycle's own screen.

Questions, problems or feedback: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

apps.name: MOTO-HUB
apps.subtitle: Map, speed and navigation on your motorcycle's screen
apps.localizedDescription:
MOTO-HUB projects a ride dashboard onto the screen built into your motorcycle.

It speaks the EasyConn protocol used by CFMOTO, Voge, Zontes, Moto Morini, Benelli, KOVE, QJ Motor and Morbidelli dashboards. Pair by scanning the QR code the dashboard shows, and the phone takes over the display: a vector map, turn-by-turn navigation with spoken directions, speed, altitude, compass, weather, trip metrics and route elevation.

WHAT YOU NEED

• A motorcycle whose dashboard supports phone projection over Wi-Fi
• iOS 17 or later

WHAT SIDELOADING COSTS YOU

These limits are Apple's, not this app's, and all three bite at the worst moment:

• You sign in with your own Apple ID. AltStore uses it to sign the app on your device. Your credentials go to Apple, not to us — there is no server on our side.
• The app stops working after 7 days unless AltStore refreshes it. Refreshing takes seconds over Wi-Fi, but it has to happen. Refresh before a long trip.
• A free Apple ID allows 3 sideloaded apps at a time, across everything you have installed this way.

A paid Apple Developer account raises the 7 days to a year and the limit to 100.

ONE THING THAT WILL NOT WORK

Joining the motorcycle's Wi-Fi automatically needs an entitlement a free Apple ID cannot carry. The app detects this, says so once, and everything else works — join the motorcycle's network by hand in Settings, then press Connect.

Maps, routing and search use free public services (OpenFreeMap, Valhalla, Photon, Open-Meteo, OpenStreetMap) and need no account. If you route often you can add your own Stadia Maps key in Settings; leaving it empty keeps the public server.

The motorcycle's Wi-Fi has no internet of its own, so map tiles travel over mobile data.

Not affiliated with CFMOTO or any motorcycle manufacturer.

While you ride, use the app's Dim button rather than locking the phone: iOS takes the video hardware back when the screen goes off, which ends the connection. Dim blacks out the phone and keeps the dashboard running.

versions.localizedDescription:
KOVE motorcycles, and a real archive for your rides.

**KOVE dashboards are now supported.** A KOVE doesn't connect like the others — it pairs over Bluetooth and then calls your phone, rather than waiting to be called. Until now MOTO-HUB searched the network for it and found nothing, forever. Scan the QR code on the dashboard as usual and the app recognises it and takes care of the rest. Say yes to the Bluetooth and Local Network prompts when they appear — without them the dashboard has no way to reach your phone.

**Trips is an archive now, not a list.** Open Trips and you get your riding year at a glance, then your months, then the rides inside them. Search by name, sort by distance or date, and hold a ride to pick out several at once.

**Tap a ride and it opens.** Before, nothing happened. Now you get the route drawn on a map you can open full screen, how far you went and how long it took, your average and top speed, how much you climbed, and the shape of the climb.

**Deleting is no longer final.** Rides go to a trash and wait there 30 days. Clear out a whole month by mistake and there is an Undo right where you did it — and the trash is the only place anything is really gone for good.

## Ride with us and tell us what breaks

MOTO-HUB for iOS is young and it is tested by the people who use it. Every fix in the last month came from someone sending a log after a ride that went wrong.

You are especially welcome if you have a **KOVE** — or a Voge, Zontes, Benelli, QJ Motor, Moto Morini or Morbidelli, which are all supported and all thin on riders.

It costs you one message. Come and say which motorcycle you ride:
**https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz**

Navigation, properly.

**A NAV section instead of a search box.** Tap NAV and you get a live map that grows when you start typing, your recent places, your favourites, and Home and Work. The app now has a proper bar at the bottom — Ride, NAV, Trips, Garage, Settings — instead of four unlabelled icons in a corner.

**See the route before you commit to it.** Distance, time and arrival; the climb ahead as a profile you can drag and pinch; where the bends are and which stretch is the best one; every turn in a list. Tap anything and the map dives to it.

**What's on the way.** Mountain passes with their height, fuel stops with how far off the road they are, speed cameras, and the weather **at the hour you'll actually get there** — "rain from 42 km, in about 35 minutes" — not the weather outside your window now.

**Plan a ride with stops.** Search or tap the map to add them, drag to reorder. Or tap any road on the route map and it redraws to pass through there.

**Places worth stopping at.** Fuel, food, coffee, viewpoints, motorcycle workshops and twenty more — on the map, tap one to ride there or keep it.

**Follow a GPX.** Import one and ride it. Saved routes now show their actual shape, so you can tell last Sunday from last month at a glance.

**When you arrive**, the app says so and offers to keep the place.

**Also:** an About page with the version, the safety notice and the links — please read it — and clearer messages when something goes wrong: no signal, a busy free server, or a destination too far away now say so instead of showing the same line.

Stuck, or it worked? Tell us: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

Your whole phone on the motorcycle's screen.

**Screen mirroring** is a new mode, next to Ride Dashboard. Start it and whatever is on your phone shows up on the dashboard — Waze, Google Maps, anything you like — and it keeps going when you switch apps.

The first time, iOS shows you a list and asks what to broadcast: pick **MOTO-HUB Screen**. It only asks once.

**Dim the phone.** A new button darkens the phone's screen while everything carries on. Press it before you switch to your navigation app. Locking the phone still ends the session, so use this instead.

**Fixed: the route was drawn in the wrong place.** On the dashboard the line sat between the streets rather than on them — right under you, wrong everywhere else. It now follows the road, and the map scrolls more smoothly.

**Can't join the motorcycle's Wi-Fi?** The app now shows you the network name and password it read from the QR code, ready to copy.

**It tells you which dashboard it connected to**, so you can tell your motorcycle apart from anything else on the network.

Stuck, or it worked? Tell us: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

Now spots the most common reason the app can't find your motorcycle: the phone quietly joined a hotspot instead.

iPhones remember networks and rejoin them on their own, and iOS never tells the app which one you're on — so being on a friend's hotspot, or your other phone's, looked exactly like being on the motorcycle. The app now recognises those networks and says so, instead of hunting for a dashboard that was never there.

Stuck, or it worked? Tell us: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

When the app can't find your motorcycle, it now tells you why.

Instead of just "no dashboard found", it checks the network you're on and says what it found: whether your motorcycle answered but isn't ready yet, or whether iOS is blocking the app from seeing it at all. Each comes with the one thing worth trying.

Stuck, or it worked? Tell us: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

Two fixes from rider reports.

• The dashboard map now moves smoothly. It was redrawing far too slowly.
• Preview gives the map back when you close it, instead of leaving the app on your dash.

Tip: hold the phone in landscape while using Preview.

Not tested on a motorcycle yet — tell us how it goes: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

Finds motorcycles that don't announce themselves.

• Some dashboards broadcast their Wi-Fi but never announce themselves on it — the app couldn't see them, and asked you to type an address you have no way of knowing. It now looks for your motorcycle on the network you're connected to.
• If it still can't find it, the message names the two things worth checking: that Local Network is allowed in Settings › MOTO-HUB, and that your phone is joined to the motorcycle's Wi-Fi.

Not tested on a motorcycle yet — let us know how it goes: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

Fixes getting stuck on "my phone hosts the hotspot".

• If a connection failed once, the app could end up asking for a Personal Hotspot forever — even when the motorcycle's own Wi-Fi was working fine. It now looks for your dashboard either way.
• If your hotspot is on but the dashboard won't join it, the app now reminds you to turn on Maximise Compatibility in Settings › Personal Hotspot.

Not tested on a motorcycle yet — let us know how it goes: https://discord.gg/q6tARNZz

A real fix for text fields that seemed unresponsive, and a shortcut to Settings when the app can't join Wi-Fi itself.

• Fixed the network name and password fields: the shared component defaulted to a numbers-and-punctuation keyboard, wrong for an ordinary Wi-Fi name. Now uses a normal keyboard everywhere except the two fields that actually need digits.
• Those fields are now larger, clearly bordered, and easier to hit — the password field finally matches the network name field instead of looking unfinished.
• An Open Settings button appears when this build can't join Wi-Fi on its own, instead of leaving you to find the right screen yourself.
• A clearer message when the scanned QR is CFMOTO/Carbit's app-download code rather than a pairing one — confirmed on a real Benelli TRK 702.

Controls, a smoother map, and a clearer message when the wrong QR gets scanned.

• Record button on the ride dashboard page, alongside Preview, Destination and Controls.
• Camera tilt on the dashboard's live map — leans into a 40° perspective as speed picks up.
• Voice guidance now actually stops when a ride ends, instead of continuing to announce turns with no visible connection to why.
• The map's position no longer jumps once a second between GPS fixes — it now moves continuously, the same technique any turn-by-turn app uses.
• Fixed a real bug that made the live map capture fail with "already recording" after backgrounding the app.
• Some dashboards show only an app-download QR with no pairing code — scanning it now says so plainly and points at manual network entry, instead of sending you to look for a screen that does not exist.

The tilt, the smoother map motion and the capture fix depend on the live map preview actually running — not yet confirmed on a motorcycle.

A fix for dashboards that connect and show nothing.

Some real dashboards tell the phone they cannot read the extra 4-byte frame index normally sent with every video frame. The phone agreed to drop it, then sent it anyway — the session looked connected while the dashboard's decoder choked on every frame, leaving the screen black or frozen.

The setting meant to honour that agreement was never wired up. It now follows the same rule the Android app uses: a recognised dashboard keeps the framing already proven on it, and only an unrecognised one is trusted to mean what it says about its own decoder.

Not yet confirmed on a motorcycle. The in-app log now says which framing was chosen for your dashboard.

Controls for the ride dashboard, and panels that can rotate through several widgets.

• A Controls page with four glove-sized tiles: cycle the side panels, throw the map fullscreen, and step either panel's widget without looking at the motorcycle.
• Tick two or more widgets for a panel and it rotates between them, from 3 seconds to a minute.
• Fixed: the map did not grow into the space a hidden panel left, leaving black bands down the sides of the dashboard.

Rewritten dashboard transport, now entirely native.

• Finds the dashboard reliably: the address is read from the Bonjour record rather than a hostname that does not resolve.
• Fixes the greeting the dashboard reads, down to the byte.
• A dashboard that answers but never connects back is now reported instead of looking connected.
• The log says what the dashboard asked for and what it was actually sent, so a failure can be diagnosed from one file.
• Optional Stadia Maps routing key in Settings.
